views.name: superhero_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  superhero.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  superhero.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
views.description: One-row-per-superhero with canonical identifying and demographic fields (joins to referenced lookup ids are kept as ids to allow flexible joins). Exposes keys and common filterable attributes used in queries about heroes.
validated_on: Among the superheroes with blue eyes, how many of them have the super power of "Agility"?
counter_examples: Which superheroes have a durability attribute value of less than 50?

views.name: hero_power_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hero_power.hero_id AS hero_id,
  hero_power.power_id AS power_id
FROM hero_power
views.description: Mapping of heroes to their powers; one row per hero-power association. Useful to list or filter powers for a given hero or aggregate powers across heroes.
validated_on: Among the superheroes with the super power of "Super Strength", how many of them have a height of over 200cm?

views.name: superpower_catalog
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superpower.id AS id,
  superpower.power_name AS power_name
FROM superpower
views.description: Catalog of superpowers with id and canonical power name. Use for lookups and final projection of power_name.
validated_on: How many heroes have stealth power?

views.name: superhero_core_3
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.gender_id AS gender_id,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  s.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  s.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  s.race_id AS race_id,
  s.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  s.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  s.height_cm AS height_cm,
  s.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero s
views.description: One-row-per-superhero with primary identifying and physical attributes and foreign keys to categorical tables. Useful as the base cohort when filtering heroes by physical traits, identity, publisher, race, alignment or colours.
counter_examples: Between DC and Marvel Comics, which publisher has published more superheroes? Find the difference in the number of superheroes they have published.

views.name: superpower_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.id AS id,
  TRIM(
    REPLACE(
      REPLACE(
        REPLACE(
          LOWER(sp.power_name),
          '\t', ' '
        ),
        '\n', ' '
      ),
      '  ', ' '
    )
  ) AS power_name
FROM superpower AS sp
views.description: Canonical list of superpowers (id + normalized power_name). Keeps power identifiers and a cleaned/trimmed name useful for equality or fuzzy matching.

views.name: colour_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  colour
FROM
  colour
views.description: Lookup table for colour id to canonical colour text. Use to join and filter superheroes (eyes/hair/skin) by human-readable colour values.
counter_examples: Rank superheroes from Marvel Comics by their eye color popularity, starting with the most common color.

views.name: hero_powers_expanded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hero_power.hero_id AS hero_id,
  hero_power.power_id AS power_id,
  superpower.power_name AS power_name
FROM hero_power
JOIN superpower ON superpower.id = hero_power.power_id
views.description: Denormalized mapping of each superhero to each of their powers with power text. One row per (hero_id, power_id, power_name). Useful to filter heroes by possession of specific powers and to aggregate counts by power.

views.name: colour_lookup_7
views.body_sql:
SELECT

views.description: Canonical colour lookup exposing colour id and normalized colour name for joins and filtering.

views.name: hero_attributes_and_powers
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS "superhero.id",
  superhero.superhero_name AS "superhero.superhero_name",
  hero_attribute.attribute_id AS "hero_attribute.attribute_id",
  hero_attribute.attribute_value AS "hero_attribute.attribute_value",
  hero_power.power_id AS "hero_power.power_id"
FROM superhero
LEFT JOIN hero_attribute
  ON hero_attribute.hero_id = superhero.id
LEFT JOIN hero_power
  ON hero_power.hero_id = superhero.id
views.description: Per-hero attribute scores and powers. Exposes each hero's attribute values and associated power ids to enable filtering, aggregation, or ranking by attributes/powers.

views.name: superhero_core_20
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS hero_id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  superhero.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  publisher.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  alignment.alignment AS alignment,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  gender.gender AS gender,
  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  eye_colour.colour AS eye_colour,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  hair_colour.colour AS hair_colour,
  superhero.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  skin_colour.colour AS skin_colour,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  race.race AS race,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
LEFT JOIN publisher ON publisher.id = superhero.publisher_id
LEFT JOIN alignment ON alignment.id = superhero.alignment_id
LEFT JOIN gender ON gender.id = superhero.gender_id
LEFT JOIN colour AS eye_colour ON eye_colour.id = superhero.eye_colour_id
LEFT JOIN colour AS hair_colour ON hair_colour.id = superhero.hair_colour_id
LEFT JOIN colour AS skin_colour ON skin_colour.id = superhero.skin_colour_id
LEFT JOIN race ON race.id = superhero.race_id
views.description: Denormalized row-level view of superheroes with their basic demographic and reference attributes (links to publisher, alignment, gender, colours, race). Useful as the primary cohort for filtering, counting, and joining to attributes or powers.
validated_on: In superheroes with height between 150 to 180, what is the percentage of heroes published by Marvel Comics?

validated_on: What are the superpowers of heroes with ID 1?

views.name: hero_attribute_values_23

counter_examples: Which superheroes have a durability attribute value of less than 50?

views.name: superhero_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sc.id AS hero_id,
  sc.superhero_name,
  sc.full_name,
  sc.gender_id,
  g.gender AS gender,
  sc.race_id,
  r.race AS race,
  sc.publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name,
  sc.alignment_id,
  a.alignment AS alignment,
  sc.eye_colour_id,
  ce.colour AS eye_colour,
  sc.hair_colour_id,
  ch.colour AS hair_colour,
  sc.skin_colour_id,
  cs.colour AS skin_colour,
  sc.height_cm,
  sc.weight_kg
FROM superhero_core sc
LEFT JOIN gender g ON sc.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON sc.race_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON sc.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON sc.alignment_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN colour ce ON sc.eye_colour_id = ce.id
LEFT JOIN colour ch ON sc.hair_colour_id = ch.id
LEFT JOIN colour cs ON sc.skin_colour_id = cs.id
views.description: Canonicalized hero-level demographic and identity information (ids and textual labels for gender, race, publisher, alignment, and colour references). Exposes basic numeric measures (height_cm, weight_kg) for grouping/filters.

views.name: hero_powers_25

FROM hero_power_link AS hpl
JOIN superhero_core AS s ON s.id = hpl.hero_id
JOIN superpower_catalog AS sp ON sp.id = hpl.power_id
views.description: Hero-to-power mapping with hero identifiers and power names. Useful to filter or group heroes by possession of specific powers.

views.name: superhero_denorm_labels
views.body_sql:
SELECT

  s.full_name AS full_name,
  g.gender AS gender,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,

  s.height_cm AS height_cm,
  s.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN colour ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
views.description: Denormalized superhero rows that replace fk ids with human-readable labels from lookup tables (gender, race, publisher, alignment, colours). One row per superhero; convenient for returning textual attributes directly.

views.name: hero_attributes_and_powers_27
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS hero_id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  a.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  attr.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  a.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  hp.power_id AS power_id,
  sp.power_name AS power_name
FROM superhero s
JOIN hero_attribute a
  ON s.id = a.hero_id
LEFT JOIN attribute attr
  ON a.attribute_id = attr.id
LEFT JOIN hero_power hp
  ON s.id = hp.hero_id
LEFT JOIN superpower sp
  ON hp.power_id = sp.id
views.description: Hero-level attributes and powers combined: each row links a superhero to one attribute (with its numeric value) and indicates associated powers. Useful for filtering or aggregating heroes by attributes or powers.

views.name: publisher_lookup_37

views.name: superhero_with_publisher_38
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN publisher p
  ON s.publisher_id = p.id
views.description: Denormalized view joining superheroes to publisher names (and optionally other small lookups). One row per superhero enriched with publisher_name to simplify counts and grouping by publisher.

views.name: publishers_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  trim(
    lower(
      replace(
        replace(
          replace(
            replace(p.publisher_name, '&', 'and'),
          '—', '-'),
        '–', '-'),
      '\t', ' ')
    )
  ) AS publisher_name_canonical
FROM publisher p
views.description: Normalized publisher rows exposing id and a cleaned canonical publisher_name for lookups and joins.

views.name: superheroes_with_publisher
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS superhero_id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  publisher.id AS publisher_id,
  publisher.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
LEFT JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id
views.description: Denormalized superhero rows joined to their publisher and demographic lookup values to support queries that filter or group by publisher attributes.

views.name: hero_attribute_values_42

SELECT
  hero_attribute.hero_id AS hero_id,

grain: hero_id, attribute_id -- one row per hero-attribute pairing
views.description: Flattened attributes per hero exposing each attribute id and its numeric value. Keeps one row per (hero_id, attribute_id) to enable aggregations (e.g., avg strength by publisher) and joins back to superhero.

views.name: superhero_basic_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.hero_id AS hero_id,
  sd.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  sd.full_name AS full_name,
  sd.gender AS gender,
  sd.race AS race,
  sd.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  sd.alignment AS alignment,
  sd.eye_colour AS eye_colour,
  sd.hair_colour AS hair_colour,
  sd.skin_colour AS skin_colour,
  sd.height_cm AS height_cm,
  sd.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero_demographics sd
views.description: One row per superhero with core demographic and physical attributes joined to normalized lookup labels (gender, race, publisher, alignment, colours). Exposes keys and raw measures for filtering, grouping, and aggregation.

views.name: hero_attribute_values_44
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ha.hero_id AS hero_id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  a.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value AS attribute_value
FROM hero_attribute ha
JOIN superhero s ON s.id = ha.hero_id
JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
views.description: One row per hero-attribute pairing providing attribute name and numeric value. Useful for filtering or aggregating heroes by attribute thresholds (e.g., high strength, intelligence).

views.name: hero_powers_45
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id AS hero_id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  sp.power_name AS power_name
FROM hero_power_link hp
JOIN superhero_core s ON s.id = hp.hero_id
JOIN superpower_catalog sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id
grain: hero_id, power_id (one row per hero-power association)
views.description: One row per hero-power association, exposing hero identifiers, hero name, and power label. Supports queries about heroes having specific powers or counting powers per hero.

views.name: superhero_core_46
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.gender_id AS gender_id,
  g.gender AS gender,
  s.race_id AS race_id,
  r.race AS race,
  s.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  s.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  a.alignment AS alignment,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  s.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,
  s.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  sc.colour AS skin_colour,
  s.height_cm AS height_cm,
  s.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN colour ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
views.description: Denormalized one-row-per-superhero with key demographic and identifying attributes joined from lookup tables (gender, race, publisher, alignment, colours). Useful as a base cohort for filtering superheroes by gender, race, publisher, alignment, or physical attributes.
validated_on: What are the superpowers of heroes with ID 1?

views.name: hero_power_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id AS hero_id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  hp.power_id AS power_id,
  sp.power_name AS power_name
FROM hero_power_link hp
JOIN superhero_core s ON s.id = hp.hero_id
JOIN superpower_catalog sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id
views.description: Row-level relation that links each hero to each of their superpowers (one row per hero-power association), with power metadata. Useful for finding powers by hero cohorts or aggregating powers across groups.
validated_on: How many heroes have stealth power?

views.name: superhero_core_48
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS superhero_id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,

  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,

  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
views.description: One-row-per-superhero with core identifying attributes and foreign keys resolved to ids for easy filtering and joining. Useful as the primary denormalized superhero relation for filters on height, weight, gender, publisher, alignment, race, and colour ids.

views.name: colour_lookup_49
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  colour.id AS colour_id,
  TRIM(LOWER(colour.colour)) AS colour
FROM colour
views.description: Canonical colour id to colour name mapping. Exposes colour id and normalized colour text for joining and direct string filters.

views.name: superhero_with_colours
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS superhero_id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg,
  eye.colour AS eye_colour,
  hair.colour AS hair_colour,
  skin.colour AS skin_colour,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  superhero.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id
FROM superhero
LEFT JOIN colour AS eye ON superhero.eye_colour_id = eye.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS hair ON superhero.hair_colour_id = hair.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS skin ON superhero.skin_colour_id = skin.id
views.description: Denormalized superhero rows including human-readable eye, hair, and skin colour names. Facilitates queries that filter or display superheroes by colour text without repeating joins.

views.name: colour_lookup_51
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  colour
FROM
  colour
views.description: Colour lookup table to translate colour id to human-readable colour text for eye/hair/skin colours.

views.name: race_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race.id AS id,
  race.race AS race
FROM race
views.description: Race lookup table exposing race id and text to filter or join by race name.

views.name: publisher_dim_53
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  publisher.id AS id,
  publisher.publisher_name AS publisher_name
FROM publisher
views.description: Publisher dimension exposing publisher id and canonical publisher name for joins and filters.

views.name: superhero_basic

SELECT

views.description: One row per superhero with primary identifying and physical attributes normalized for querying (names, gender, height, weight and foreign-key ids).

views.name: gender_lookup_55
views.body_sql:

  gender.id AS id,
  gender.gender AS gender
FROM gender
views.description: Mapping of gender id to canonical gender text for easy joins and filters by gender label.

views.name: superhero_weight_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(s.id) AS count_heroes,
  AVG(s.weight_kg) AS avg_weight_kg,
  MIN(s.weight_kg) AS min_weight_kg,
  MAX(s.weight_kg) AS max_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
views.description: Aggregate weight statistics across all superheroes to support comparisons against population averages (raw measures, count, avg, min, max, stddev if available).

views.name: attribute_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  attribute.id AS id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name
FROM attribute
views.description: Canonical attribute reference exposing attribute id and name for joining and filtering attributes (e.g., Strength, Intelligence).

views.name: superhero_basic_58
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS superhero_id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  superhero.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  publisher.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  alignment.alignment AS alignment,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  gender.gender AS gender,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  race.race AS race,
  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  superhero.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
LEFT JOIN publisher ON publisher.id = superhero.publisher_id
LEFT JOIN alignment ON alignment.id = superhero.alignment_id
LEFT JOIN gender ON gender.id = superhero.gender_id

LEFT JOIN colour AS eye_colour ON eye_colour.id = superhero.eye_colour_id
LEFT JOIN colour AS hair_colour ON hair_colour.id = superhero.hair_colour_id
LEFT JOIN colour AS skin_colour ON skin_colour.id = superhero.skin_colour_id
views.description: One-row-per-superhero with core identifying and demographic attributes plus foreign-key ids resolved for joins (keeps publisher, alignment, gender and colour/race ids and raw height/weight). Useful as the main superhero entity for filtering, grouping and joining to attributes/powers.

views.name: hero_attribute_facts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hero_attribute.hero_id AS hero_id,
  hero_attribute.hero_id AS superhero_id,
  hero_attribute.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  hero_attribute.attribute_value AS attribute_value
FROM hero_attribute
JOIN attribute ON attribute.id = hero_attribute.attribute_id
grain: hero_attribute.hero_id + hero_attribute.attribute_id (one row per hero-attribute pair)
views.description: One-row-per-hero-attribute association exposing attribute metadata together with the raw numeric attribute_value. Useful for finding heroes by particular attribute names and comparing or aggregating attribute values.

views.name: hero_power_joined
views.body_sql:

JOIN superpower ON superpower.id = hero_power.power_id
views.description: Hero-to-power mapping with power names; one row per hero-power. Useful for filtering heroes by powers or counting/distinct-ing powers per hero.

views.name: superhero_core_dimensions
views.body_sql:

views.name: superhero_attribute_matrix
views.body_sql:

views.description: Hero attributes pivoted to one row per hero with attribute_name columns and their numeric values. Useful for queries comparing Intelligence/Strength/etc. across heroes or filtering by attribute thresholds.

views.name: hero_powers_flat

views.description: Flat mapping of heroes to their powers (one row per hero-power) including power name and hero basic identifiers. Useful for filtering heroes by specific powers or counting powers per hero.

views.name: superhero_basic_64
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,

  gender.gender AS gender,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,

  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  alignment.alignment AS alignment,
  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  superhero.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
LEFT JOIN gender ON superhero.gender_id = gender.id
LEFT JOIN race ON superhero.race_id = race.id
LEFT JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id
LEFT JOIN alignment ON superhero.alignment_id = alignment.id
views.description: One row per superhero with denormalized reference ids and names from related dimension tables (gender, race, publisher, alignment) and raw physical attributes (height, weight) and colour ids.

views.name: hero_powers_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id AS hero_id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  hp.power_id AS power_id,
  sp.power_name AS power_name,
  ha.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  a.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value AS attribute_value
FROM hero_power hp
JOIN superhero s ON s.id = hp.hero_id
JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id
JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
grain: hero_id, power_id, attribute_id  -- combination rows linking a hero to a power and an attribute value
views.description: Mapping of heroes to their powers and attribute scores; one row per hero-power-attribute combination to support queries that need hero features, skill tallies, or to filter heroes by having particular powers or attribute values.
